response.markdown_report:
## Insights and directions

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Industrial and Electronics have wrong-rank rates of 12.25% and 11.27%; their negative lower-tail margins motivate improving difficult predictions. These training diagnostics do not establish validation performance. (2) Users report both stale-interest recommendations and broadly relevant items they would defer. Learning the immediate next choice could address both failures. (3) Embedding scores near 0.5 imply approximately zero mean cosine similarity. Collapse regularization therefore lacks diagnostic support.

**Literature insights.** (1) [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) already uses last-item masking to reduce training–inference mismatch. Prefix-terminal supervision is a feasible extension of that established practice. (2) [gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192) motivates investigating negative coverage and objective calibration without adopting its backbone. (3) [AHNS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.05191) motivates controlling hardness because difficult negatives can include plausible positives; transfer to masked recommendation remains unproven.

## Framework and candidate ideas

| Direction | Atomic experiment | Intended failure addressed |
|---|---|---|
| Prediction alignment | Increase prefix-terminal supervision | Historical relevance outweighs present choice |
| Candidate discrimination | Gradually introduce moderate hard negatives | Confusing candidates outrank positives |
| Item specificity | Jointly learn gated title/description embeddings | Broad resemblance obscures specific connections |

Scores below are originality / potential / user alignment / model alignment / difficulty; difficulty 10 means hardest. Alignment scores express hypotheses, not measured gains.

- **Prefix-terminal supervision: 3/7/8/7/2.** Originality + tests a targeted mixture; − terminal masking is established. Potential + cheap and reusable; − effects may saturate. User + targets stale interests and deferred broad matches; − cannot establish compatibility. Model + directly supervises next-choice separation; − margin gains remain uncertain. Difficulty + small sampling change; − requires leakage checks.
- **Moderate-negative curriculum: 4/7/6/9/5.** Originality + transfers controlled hardness; − well-studied principle. Potential + targets lower-tail errors; − false negatives persist. User + may distinguish close alternatives; − hardness does not encode usefulness. Model + directly targets wrong ranks; − can overfit sampled candidates. Difficulty + preserves architecture; − mining adds cost.
- **Gated text embeddings: 4/6/8/6/6.** Originality + compliant joint text learning; − established multimodal pattern. Potential + represents specific attributes; − sparse supervision. User + may capture model identifiers and artists; − text does not reveal ownership. Model + may separate similar IDs; − unverified. Difficulty + one network; − tokenization and predictor changes.

## Selected experiment

At 0% progress, choose **prefix-terminal supervision**. It explicitly targets stale historical preferences and broadly plausible recommendations lacking an immediate-choice connection, while addressing weak positive–negative separation. Alternate terminal and interior reconstruction batches equally, averaging each batch’s supervised-token loss. For terminal batches, sample a training-history target, discard its suffix, and replace it with MASK.

Retain one BERT4Rec checkpoint/category, unchanged routing and evaluator, seeds 0/42, and 200 epochs × 200 batches. Use left padding, appended-mask inference, and final-nonpadding readout. Select by macro validation HR@10; report diagnostic changes separately. Compatibility and quantity errors remain unresolved without reliable supporting evidence.

idea.description: Increase inference-aligned prefix-terminal supervision within the corrected BERT4Rec baseline, alternating terminal and interior masked reconstruction batches in one jointly trained model per category.
idea.motivation: User feedback identifies stale historical interests and broadly plausible but deferrable recommendations. Training directly on immediate next choices may address these two failures. Negative lower-tail margins in Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics motivate testing whether this supervision also improves difficult candidate separation.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve the supplied backbone, loss, optimizer and sampling except for the masking-policy experiment. For terminal examples, choose a target index from the training history with at least one preceding interaction; remove every subsequent interaction and replace the target with the reserved mask token. Interior examples must replace every supervised target with MASK, avoiding shifted-target leakage. Alternate batch types 1:1 and average losses over supervised positions. Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], four-category routing, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Save artifacts beneath the trial directory. Retain one checkpoint per category and the baseline predictor writer; serialize any changed masking configuration. Keep DiagnosisProbe and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt interfaces. Diagnostic margins must be measured at genuinely masked positions; unavailable category breakdowns should be marked unavailable. No validation improvement is claimed before host evaluation.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
    model = corrected_baseline_BERT4Rec(category)
    for epoch in range(200):
        for step in range(200):
            histories = sample_training_histories()
            if step % 2 == 0:
                # Index sampling uses training histories only.
                examples = []
                for history in histories:
                    t = sample_target_index(history, minimum_index=1)
                    target = history[t]
                    prefix = history[:t][- (MAXLEN - 1):]
                    sequence = left_pad(prefix + [MASK], MAXLEN)
                    examples.append((sequence, MAXLEN - 1, target))
            else:
                examples = baseline_interior_masked_examples(histories)
            features = model.log2feats(examples.sequence)
            loss = baseline_loss_at_supervised_positions(features, examples).mean()
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
        baseline_validation_and_checkpoint_selection()
    save_one_selected_checkpoint_and_matching_predictor(category)
# Inference: left_pad(history[-(MAXLEN-1):] + [MASK]); read final nonpadding position.

originality.positive: A focused experiment on prefix-terminal supervision and balanced objective weighting is tailored to the observed immediate-choice failures.
originality.negative: Last-item masking and the training–inference mismatch are already discussed in BERT4Rec; this is an incremental experiment.

future_potential.positive: A low-cost objective change can establish a useful foundation before adding text features or harder negatives.
future_potential.negative: The baseline may already contain sufficient terminal supervision, and immediate-choice training cannot independently establish equipment compatibility.

code_difficulty.positive: Primarily changes training-example construction while preserving the network and inference architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Requires careful target exclusion, left-padding handling, loss normalization and masked-position diagnostics.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item learning for sequential recommendation.
Includes last-item masking to improve alignment with next-item inference.
limitations: Terminal masking is established prior art, limiting the proposed experiment's novelty.
Its results do not establish the best masking mixture for this fixed Amazon benchmark.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Examines sampled-BCE overconfidence and motivates improved negative coverage and objective calibration.
limitations: Uses a different backbone; only the objective-design motivation transfers here.
Does not establish gains for the proposed BERT4Rec masking-policy experiment.

related_work.title: Adaptive Hardness Negative Sampling for Collaborative Filtering
contributions: Motivates adaptive negative hardness to manage problems associated with fixed hardness.
limitations: Evidence concerns collaborative filtering rather than this masked sequential benchmark.
Hardness alone does not establish compatibility or eliminate false negatives.
